summary: Port reproduces the pattern's mechanism exactly — stationary twinkles that pop to full white or full primary-colour and decay exponentially at randomised rates — and matches the original statistically at every dialed setting; the visible gaps are all in the UNTOUCHED defaults (primary hue 324 deg vs 306 deg, a faster default speed) plus a missing ~2 s opening flash and a thinner white-sparkle share.
observations: Rig: strip, 60 px. Both sides compile and run clean, no runtime errors, no sensor use (wantsSensors false on both). Neither side drifts, decays or freezes: brightnessTrend 'steady' on both over 60 s and 240 s surveys, zeroMotionFrames 1 (the unavoidable first frame).

Same mechanism on both sides, confirmed by dumping 200 consecutive frames (--label longdump, 20 s..29.95 s at 20 fps): individual pixels ignite at full 255, then decay multiplicatively in place with no spatial movement (waterfall = pure vertical streaks, never slanted). Two populations on BOTH sides: pure-white fairies (255/255/255 -> grey ramp) and primary-colour fairies (255/0/B -> fading ramp), and each fairy gets its own decay rate, giving a mix of short stubs and long tails.

Untouched default primary colour differs: original's colour fairies ignite at exactly 255/0/229 (hue 306 deg, i.e. magenta-violet) on every event; the port's at 255/0/153 (hue 324 deg, rose-pink). Constant across the whole run on both sides, and visible in the survey waterfalls as violet-magenta vs pink-crimson.

The picker itself is faithful: with hsvPickerPrimaryColor pinned to the SAME value on both sides the ignition chromaticity is byte-identical (0.33,1,1 -> both 0/255/0 family; 0.66,0.5,1 -> both the same blue family, including both sides ignoring the s=0.5 component the same way). So the divergence is the default value, not the colour math.

Untouched default speed differs. At default controls the original spawns 8.0 ignitions/s with mean brightness half-life 0.83 s; the port spawns 11.4/s with half-life 0.69 s (measured over 60 px x 10 s, n=80 vs n=114 ignition events). Cross-referencing the pinned-speed sweep, the original's untouched state sits at roughly sliderSpeed 0.47 and the port's at roughly 0.33 — the port runs visibly busier and shorter-lived out of the box.

With sliderSpeed pinned equal the two converge: at 0.25 orig 10.1 ign/s vs port 12.4, half-life 13.9 vs 12.1 frames; at 0.5 orig 7.8 vs port 8.4, 18.9 vs 18.2 frames; at 0.75 orig 4.8 vs port 6.4, 24.1 vs 24.4 frames. Residual: the port spawns ~15-30% more events per second at the same setting, and its slowest-decaying fairies are shorter (max half-life 22/33/45 frames on the original vs 19/27/37 on the port at 0.25/0.5/0.75).

White-vs-coloured mix differs systematically: white ignitions are 36-44% of all ignitions on the original (0.375, 0.36, 0.36, 0.44 across four measured configurations) against a flat 28-30% on the port. The port therefore reads slightly less 'sparkly' and more uniformly pink.

Startup transient exists only on the original. At t=0 the original has ~28 of 60 pixels ALL sitting at full 255 simultaneously (mean brightness 82) and they decay together into the steady state over ~2 s; the port starts with its fairies already staggered at random mid-decay levels (mean brightness 19-20 at t=0, no flash). Both settle to the same ~24-26 mean brightness afterwards.

Steady-state texture: the original is burstier. Over matched post-transient windows its mean-brightness standard deviation is 5.5-7.3 against the port's 4.1-5.4, and its extremes are wider (survey after 10 s: orig 9-49, port 13-35). Consistent with the original's fewer but longer-tailed fairies.

Both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped: spawn rate and half-life in SECONDS hold across --fps 10 / 20 / 40 (orig 8.8/8.0/8.0 per s, half-life 0.87/0.83/0.80 s; port 10.8/11.4/10.2 per s, half-life 0.73/0.69/0.68 s). No frame-rate coupling on either side.

No mode or long-cycle structure on either side: a 240 s / 2 fps survey shows one homogeneous regime throughout, statistically stationary, on both sides. Behaviour is unchanged at seeds 7 and 1234 (orig mean brightness 26.8/24.9, port 22.4/21.3, both 'steady'), so none of the above is a one-seed fluke.
Control surfaces match exactly: both sides expose hsvPickerPrimaryColor (hsvPicker, label PrimaryColor) and sliderSpeed (slider, label Speed). No missing, extra, renamed or re-kinded control.

dials.name: hsvPickerPrimaryColor
dials.origEffect: Sets the colour of the non-white fairies; ignition RGB tracks the picker hue exactly (0.33 -> green, 0.66 -> blue). White fairies are unaffected and stay white at every setting. Untouched default is hue 306 deg (255/0/229).
dials.portEffect: Identical: same hue mapping, same byte-identical ignition colours at matched picker values, white fairies likewise unaffected. Only the untouched default differs — hue 324 deg (255/0/153).

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Inverse dial: low values give many short-lived fairies (0 -> motion stat 7, dense stubby streaks), high values give fewer, much longer-lived ones (1 -> motion 2, long tapering streaks). Measured 10.1 ign/s and 0.70 s half-life at 0.25 falling to 4.8 ign/s and 1.21 s at 0.75.
dials.portEffect: Same direction, same magnitude, same waterfall character at both extremes (motion 8 at 0, 2 at 1). 12.4 ign/s / 0.61 s at 0.25 down to 6.4 ign/s / 1.22 s at 0.75 — decay timing matches within a few percent, spawn rate runs ~15-30% high. Untouched default sits lower on the dial than the original's.

feedback: Change the default primary colour. The original's untouched colour fairies ignite at exactly RGB 255/0/229 (hue 0.85 of the wheel, saturation 1, value 1); the port's ignite at 255/0/153 (hue 0.90). Shift the default hue down by 0.05 and the untouched look matches. The picker math itself is already correct — do not touch it.

Lower the default speed. Untouched, the original produces 8.0 fairy ignitions per second on a 60 px strip with a mean brightness half-life of 0.83 s; the port produces 11.4/s with 0.69 s. On the port's own dial that means its untouched default sits near sliderSpeed 0.33 while the original's sits near 0.47 — raise the default so the untouched render slows to the original's rate.

Add the opening flash. The original ignites ~28 of 60 pixels at full brightness on frame 0 all at once (mean brightness 82) and lets them decay together into the steady state over about 2 s; the port starts with its fairies pre-staggered at random mid-decay levels (mean brightness 19). Initialise every fairy at full brightness rather than at a random phase of its decay.

Raise the white-fairy share. Across four separately-measured configurations the original made 36-44% of its ignitions pure white; the port is pinned at 28-30%. Roughly one in every 2.7 fairies should be white on the original against the port's one in 3.4.

Widen the slow tail of the decay-rate distribution. At every matched speed setting the port's longest-lived fairies die sooner than the original's — max observed half-life 19 vs 22 frames at speed 0.25, 27 vs 33 at 0.5, 37 vs 45 at 0.75 (20 fps) — while medians agree. The port's per-fairy decay rate is drawn from too narrow a range; extend it toward slower decays so the occasional long streak appears. This is also what makes the original's mean brightness swing wider (sd 5.5-7.3 vs the port's 4.1-5.4).

Trim the spawn rate slightly at matched dials: at the same sliderSpeed the port emits ~15-30% more ignitions per second than the original (12.4 vs 10.1 at 0.25, 6.4 vs 4.8 at 0.75). Secondary to the items above.

Nothing needs fixing in the core mechanism, motion or timing model: stationary in-place twinkles, exponential per-pixel decay, dual white/coloured populations, fps-invariant timing and steady long-run behaviour are all already correct.
